title: It doesn't take 21 days to build a habit
sources: Maxwell Maltz, Psycho-Cybernetics (1960): patients took a minimum of about 21 days to adjust

Lally, van Jaarsveld, Potts & Wardle (2010), European Journal of Social Psychology: 96 volunteers, 18-254 days to automaticity, median 66; missing one opportunity did not materially affect habit formation
teyro.app: streak freezes cover a busy day, a repair saves a slip

lines.text: It doesn't take *21 days* to build a habit. | Here's what the research *actually* found.
First, *21 days* came from a *plastic surgeon* in the *1960s,* | describing how long his patients took to adjust after surgery. | It was never a *study.*
Second, when *UCL* researchers tracked *96* people building a new daily habit, | it took anywhere from *18* to *254* days. | A typical habit took *66.*
Third, *missing one day* | didn't break anything. | The habit kept *building* anyway.
And finally, what mattered was doing it *most days,* | in the *same* situation. | Not being *perfect.*
So stop counting to twenty-one. | Pick a time, | keep it *small,* | and forgive a *missed* day.
That's why every streak comes with *freezes* for busy days. | Go to teyro dot app, | or just search *Teyro.*
